theme: 3 terms on table views: the scrolling list of rows, the name that tells it which kind of cell to recycle, and the recycling itself

terms.definition: A scrolling list of rows in UIKit, in one column, often grouped into sections.
terms.example: Settings is just a grouped Table View, nothing custom.
terms.code:
import UIKit
let table = UITableView(
    frame: .zero, style: .insetGrouped)
table.rowHeight = 56

terms.definition: A string that names a kind of cell, so the table knows which cells it can recycle for a row.
terms.example: The Reuse Identifier in code doesn't match the storyboard, so dequeue crashes.

terms.definition: When a list recycles cells that scrolled off screen for new rows, instead of making new ones.
terms.example: The image flickers because of Cell Reuse, cancel the old download in `prepareForReuse`.

video.description:
Learn to explain how a table view recycles its rows: Table View, Reuse Identifier & Cell Reuse, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Table View - A scrolling list of rows in UIKit, in one column, often grouped into sections.
Reuse Identifier - A string that names a kind of cell, so the table knows which cells it can recycle for a row.
Cell Reuse - When a list recycles cells that scrolled off screen for new rows, instead of making new ones.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Scroll down, and random rows get a checkmark. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Who checked that task?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, when I scroll, random tasks show a checkmark.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's Cell Reuse. The Table View recycles cells that leave the screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So a cell can come back with an old checkmark?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. You set it when `done` is true, but you never clear it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is the Reuse Identifier wrong, then?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, the Reuse Identifier only picks the cell type. `Task` is fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I add an `else` that removes the checkmark?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, or reset it in `prepareForReuse`. Cell Reuse needs a full reset.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does the Table View call that every time?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right before a reused cell comes back from the queue.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. With Cell Reuse, every row sets its whole state.
Settings screens are mostly one grouped Table View.
